questions.prompt: How do problem-directed and response-directed actions differ?
questions.answer: One aims to alter the demand; the other supports functioning or manages its effects.
No; it can support functioning while a problem is addressed or cannot yet be changed.
To decide whether the demand changed, the plan is manageable or further support is needed.

questions.prompt: What takes priority in a threatening situation?
questions.answer: Safety and appropriate assistance rather than a general coping exercise.
questions.feedback: Do not substitute a worksheet for support.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Selects proportionate problem-directed and response-directed actions, with consent, review and escalation boundaries.
scoring.transfer: Prepare a two-column coping choice worksheet for two fictional demands, one modifiable and one currently outside the learner's control. Include safe alternatives, a review date and an escalation condition. Explain why doing more is not always the best response.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
